In early 2024, security researchers leveraged AI-assisted analysis tools to uncover previously undetected vulnerabilities in curl, one of the most widely deployed networking libraries in existence. The tool, utilizing large language models trained on code patterns and security weaknesses, identified edge cases in curl's HTTP header parsing logic that had survived decades of manual code review. These findings highlight a fundamental shift in how security auditing can be performed at scale.
Traditional code review relies on human pattern recognition, often guided by known vulnerabil…

A scope management plan is an essential document in project management that ensures a project stays within its defined boundaries. It provides clarity on what the project will deliver, how the deliverables will be produced, and how any changes will be managed. Without a scope management plan, projects are more likely to face challenges such as scope creep, miscommunication, and delays, which can affect overall success.
The purpose of a scope management plan is to create a structured approach for defining and managing project objectives. It serves as a reference point for all stakeholders, setting expectations about what is included in the project and what lies outside its boundaries. This prevents unnecessary confusion and ensures that every team member understands their rol…

articles.description:
Moloch the judger of social credit


GPT-2's unexpected abilities suggest AGI could emerge accidentally from current AI systems, challenging assumptions about artificial intelligence limitations.
A meta-analysis shows cognitive skills don't transfer between domains - smarter people excel at chess, but chess instruction doesn't make people smarter.
The MBTI test relies on false opposites in two of its four dimensions, with thinking/feeling and sensing/intuition not being actual psychological opposites.
Misinformation persists when people lack immediate feedback about false beliefs, and incentive misalignment can lead to harmful outcomes like anti-arrhythmic drugs causing heart attacks.
👉 Read full article

articles.description:
During the final SDLC iteration of the Poor Man's Queue (Building a Poor Man's Queue with Cloudflare Workers), I encountered a subtle trap in applying SOLID principles: misguided abstraction.
While SOLID principles are designed to guide us toward maintainable code, I've observed—in my own work and others'—that we can sometimes violate their very intent by misunderstanding them. The result? Either over-engineered solutions that add complexity without value, or over-simplified solutions that sacrifice maintainability.
The original Poor Man's Queue suffered from over-abstraction, featuring three layers where two would suffice:
Queue → Queue Service → Durable Object Queue
By eliminating the unnecessary middle Queue Service layer, I created a cleaner, more maintainable architecture while still …

Have you ever stopped to think about why companies ask you to fill out forms when you request a service? Or in today’s app-driven world, why so many platforms encourage you to log in using Facebook, Google, or Twitter rather than just a simple email? At first glance, this seems like an extra cost for businesses—after all, they have to support multiple login methods. Yet, companies actively push for these options. Why?

All of this becomes the foundation for building what marketers call a buyer p…
